title: Routing fallback compatibility protocol and validation runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Maintain an automated, auditable compatibility protocol for fallback model variants used by smart routing. This ticket codifies a runbook and validation checks for tokenizer parity, context/sequence-length contract compatibility, KV cache semantics, and ancillary tooling (export/import, quantized artifacts). The goal is to ensure safe automatic fallback routing without silent regressions to tokenization or decoding behavior, and to provide deterministic remediation steps and telemetry to detect divergence. Scope: (1) automated compatibility checks as a CI gating step for model onboarding and variant publishing; (2) periodic sweep job to detect drift across active fallback cohorts; (3) operator runbook for remediating incompatible variants and issuing safe rollbacks; (4) telemetry dashboards and alerting thresholds for tokenization mismatch, off-by-one context errors, and kv-cache miss/poison rates. This ticket focuses on engineering deliverables (scripts, CI hooks, monitoring) and integrates with the existing compatibility registry and smart routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'compatibility-gate' added to model onboarding pipeline that runs tokenizer parity tests, context-length contract checks, and KV-cache smoke tests
Automated weekly sweep job that compares active serving variants against registry baseline and emits a compatibility report to the routing team channel
Runbook document with step-by-step remediation actions for (a) tokenizer mismatches, (b) context truncation regressions, (c) KV cache incompatibility, and (d) tooling serialization format mismatches
Dashboards and alerts created: tokenization-diff-rate, context-truncate-rate, kv-cache-miss-spike; alerting thresholds and on-call playbooks defined
Demo of safe fallback flow: forced variant failure triggers routing to fallback variant and circuit-breaker prevents silent degraded outputs; validated on staging with sample workloads
tasks: Design CI compatibility test spec (tokenizer golden sets, edge-case prompts, sequence-length boundary checks)
Implement tokenizer parity runner using tokenizer snapshots and normalized detokenization checks
Add context-contract validator that asserts model will accept pinned max_seq_len with expected truncation semantics
Create KV-cache semantic smoke tests (KV persistence, retrieval ordering, key collision heuristics)
Integrate checks into model onboarding pipeline and block variant publish on failures
Build weekly sweep lambda that compares serving variants to registry baselines and writes findings to S3/reporting
Create Grafana dashboards and define Prometheus metrics and alerts
Author operator runbook and include example GitHub PRs and rollback commands
Add telemetry tags to routing decisions for post-incident analysis
Coordinate validation with Solutions Eng for customer-facing fallback use-cases
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and routing teams. Agreed on three test pillars: tokenizer parity, context contract, KV semantics.
2026-02-24: Prototype tokenizer parity runner that hashes detokenized output for golden prompts; initial false positives due to whitespace normalization noted.
2026-03-02: Added normalization layer to parity checks (unicode NFKC + whitespace canonicalization). False positives dropped in local runs.
2026-03-05: Context-contract validator spec reviewed with Runtime (Diego). Decided to assert both max_seq_len acceptance and deterministic truncation behavior for sequences exceeding soft limit.
2026-03-08: Implemented KV-cache smoke test harness; discovered one variant with differing KV key hashing that caused cache misses in a micro-batch scenario. Patch proposed in PR #1245.
2026-03-10: CI integration draft merged to staging; initial runs flagged two unpublished variants. Weekly sweep job skeleton deployed to staging cluster. Next: dashboards and runbook write-up.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly strict tokenizer parity may block valid model variants due to insignificant whitespace differences. Mitigation: normalization layer and tunable similarity threshold; allow opt-out with documented rationale.

Risk: KV-cache semantic differences could be subtle and surface only under specific batching patterns. Mitigation: include micro-batch fixtures in smoke tests and add randomized stress runs during onboarding.

Risk: Increased onboarding latency from extra CI checks. Mitigation: run heavy tests asynchronously but gate public release on passing critical checks; provide 'fast-track' for enterprise partners with preflight certs.
Risk: Alert fatigue from sweep job false positives. Mitigation: aggregate findings, only escalate when correlated with routing errors or high customer-impact signals.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Enable compatibility-gate in model-onboarding pipeline for internal variants only. Run weekly sweep daily for 2 weeks to gather baselines.
Phase 2 (canary): Enable gate for 10% of new variant publishes to hosted region-us with feature-flagged auto-fallback disabled; manual review required for failures.
Phase 3 (enforce): Gate turned on for all publishes; auto-fallback allowed only for variants that pass compatibility checks. Runbook and dashboards live in production.
Rollback: If gating causes severe throughput regressions, disable gate and run focused remediation; use annotated registry to temporarily pin-serving variants.
notes_for_oncall: If tokenization-diff-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes, run 'compat-report' for affected cohort and escalate to runtime-owner.
Context-truncate-rate spikes usually indicate mismatched max_seq_len; check model metadata and recent variant publishes. If publish occurred in last 24h, rollback to previous variant key.
KV-cache-miss-spike correlated with increased latency — route affected traffic to higher-tier pool and open incident with runtime team.
